title: Outbox runtime
concern: The transactional outbox: the queue table, the claim and lease protocol, the delivery worker and the live event source, the same for every service.

title: Controller runtime
concern: The reconciliation loop: the keyed and FIFO queues, scanning and streaming of sources, retries, sweeps, the metrics collector and the per-operation telemetry, the same for every service.

title: Telemetry runtime
concern: The OpenTelemetry runtime: providers, export, the HTTP and RPC span wrappers, request metrics and completion logs, the same for every service.

title: Tenant runtime
concern: The tenant wall: the distinct Tenant type, the context accessor, the transaction helper that sets the transaction-local tenant, the per-tenant iterator for workers and controllers, the owner-role connector for migrations and the pooler compatibility guard, the same for every service. The tenant model is one level and no tenant-less path exists. It is one package of the runtime module, released with the common registry and pinned by the archetype (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R04). It is a library, not a framework: generated code calls its functions and types, and the package calls back into no generated code and owns no main loop.

title: Audit runtime
concern: The audit record: the audit.Event type, the canonical encoder and redaction, the SHA-256 hash chain, the RFC 6902 differ, the write inside the caller's transaction and the outcome write for a denied or failed mutation, the audit-sink port and its outbox destination, the anchor publisher, the verifier, the partition maintenance job and the reject-trigger DDL text, the same for every service. The default level is change, and reads of entities that hold pii are audited. It is one package of the runtime module, released with the common registry and pinned by the archetype (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R04). It is a library, not a framework: generated code calls its functions and types, and the package calls back into no generated code and owns no main loop.

title: Authorization runtime
concern: The authorization port: the decision and relationships port interfaces in the shape of OpenID AuthZEN 1.0, the consistency floor, the per-row token, the SpiceDB provider, the FIFO relay destination, the identity-to-subject mapping, the caveat context, the slot-facing handle bound to one transaction and tenant, and the conformance suite every provider passes, the same for every service. A deny is a decision; minimize-latency does not exist. It is one package of the runtime module, released with the common registry and pinned by the archetype (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R04). It is a library, not a framework: generated code calls its functions and types, and the package calls back into no generated code and owns no main loop.

title: Idempotency runtime
concern: The inbound idempotency key: the idempotency_keys table migration, the transaction wrapper that records the key with the write and replays the stored response, the canonical JSON fingerprint, the derived outgoing key, the purge job and the conformance tests, the same for every service. The key is required on create, retention is 24 h, and a replay is byte for byte. It is one package of the runtime module, released with the common registry and pinned by the archetype (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R04). It is a library, not a framework: generated code calls its functions and types, and the package calls back into no generated code and owns no main loop.

title: Money and ledger runtime
concern: The money and the ledger: the Money type at stego.dev/runtime/money (int64 minor units with an ISO 4217 code, allocation that loses no minor unit), and at stego.dev/runtime/ledger the balance derivation, the normal-balance arithmetic, the two-phase state machine and its error set, idempotent transfer replay, the reversal rules, the snapshot and ledger_check jobs and the guard trigger text, the same for every service. One currency per ledger, a pending transfer is immutable, and no difference adjustment exists. It is one package of the runtime module, released with the common registry and pinned by the archetype (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R04). It is a library, not a framework: generated code calls its functions and types, and the package calls back into no generated code and owns no main loop.

title: Lease and modes runtime
concern: The composition of one binary: at stego.dev/runtime/modes the mode registry, the flag parsing, the readiness and the shutdown sequencer per mode, and at stego.dev/runtime/lease the lease client with fencing tokens, the same for every service. The SKIP LOCKED claim loop for outbox and job rows (ST-STD-TXN-R14) stays in the Outbox runtime (ST-SUP-RP01); this package holds the lease, not the claim. The mode all is allowed in production and is the default. It is one package of the runtime module, released with the common registry and pinned by the archetype (ST-STD-RUNTIME-R04). It is a library, not a framework: generated code calls its functions and types, and the package calls back into no generated code and owns no main loop.
